title_en: MacroVoices #552 David Rosenberg: Navigating The Noise
title_zh: MacroVoices #552 David Rosenberg（Rosenberg Research）：穿越噪音
subtitle_zh: David Rosenberg 力排通胀恐慌，剖析 Fed 换届、中期选举僵局与债市机会。
summary_zh: 本期 MacroVoices 由 Patrick Ceresna 对话 Rosenberg Research 创始人、畅销书作者 David Rosenberg（新书《Bear in the Bullring》、加拿大 TSX 上市的 Rosie ETF）。在几乎所有人都倒向通胀论者（inflationist）甚至通胀恐慌论者之际，Rosie 力排众议，认为通胀被媒体与华尔街研报夸大了。他的核心论据是：正是这批人去年因 Trump 关税而高呼商品与进口通胀，但净有效关税率（net effective tariff rate）录得 1930 年代中期以来最大升幅，核心商品 CPI 同比却从 1.5% 跌到 0.7% 以下的四年低点——关税冲击本质上像一次加税，除非劳动力市场配合、渗进工资，否则不可持续；既然如此，凭什么能源这匹「独角戏」就能引发持续通胀？节目还剖析美联储政权更迭（regime change）与 Warsh 上任后收益率的重定价、中期选举后两党分立僵局的历史规律（80% 概率经济放缓、通胀下行、债券收益率走低）、房市衰退（新房均价同比跌 8.5%），以及 30 万亿美元债券抛售的变化速度问题。结尾 Trading Desk 由 Patrick Ceresna 与 Michelle Bagnan 复盘 NASDAQ 投机性净多头升至第 100 百分位的持仓转向。

turns.en: Historically, when a one-party power swings to a two-party system with gridlock, 80 percent of the time the economy slows, 80 percent of the time inflation goes down, and 80 percent of the time bond yields go down in that two-year period after a national election.
turns.zh: 从历史看，当一党独大的格局在一场全国性选举后转为两党分立、相互掣肘的僵局时，有80%的概率经济会放缓，有80%的概率通胀会下行，也有80%的概率债券收益率会在选举后的那两年里走低。

turns.en: That was Rosenberg Research founder David Rosenberg. I'm Eric Townsend, and this is Macrovoices, the free weekly podcast targeting professional finance and sophisticated private investors.
turns.zh: 刚才这段话出自 Rosenberg Research 的创始人 David Rosenberg。我是 Eric Townsend，这里是 MacroVoices，一档面向专业金融人士和成熟私人投资者的免费周更播客。

turns.en: Episode 552 was produced October 1st, 2026. Listener response to our Macrovoices Unplugged Bonus episode that gave you a double dose of Michael every last week was overwhelmingly positive.
turns.zh: 第552期节目制作于2026年10月1日。听众对我们那期 MacroVoices Unplugged 加更反响极其热烈——那期在上周给了大家双倍剂量的 Michael。

turns.zh: 所以在我们和 Rosie 深入开聊之前，先做一个简短的运营公告。往后，对于像 Michael 和 Anas Alhajji 这样话太多、一期节目根本装不下的嘉宾，我们会考虑加做 MacroVoices Unplugged 加更。

The next likely one would be when we bring Dr. Anas Alhaji back, and you can expect that before the end of the year, certainly and maybe even before the end of this month.
turns.zh: 但出于对你们时间的尊重，也坦白讲出于对我们制作预算的考虑，只有在情况确实需要时我们才会这么做。下一期很可能会做的，是我们把 Anas Alhajji 博士请回来的那期，你们可以期待它在年底前、甚至很可能在这个月底前就上线。

turns.en: We've got to work that into our schedule. That would come complete with an Unplugged Bonus episode, and get this, if you want to influence the content of that Unplugged Session, be sure to follow Anas on X because he's going to reach out to his audience for questions and topics that they want answered when we bring him back for that Unplugged Session.
turns.zh: 我们得把它排进日程。那一期同样会配一期 Unplugged 加更，而且听着，如果你想影响那期 Unplugged 专场的内容，一定要在 X 上关注 Anas，因为他会向自己的粉丝征集问题和想让我们回答的话题，等我们把他请回来做那期 Unplugged 专场时用。

turns.en: It's still a few weeks away, so you've got time now to make your request known to Anas by tweeting them. Don't send them to us because Anas is collecting that information.
turns.zh: 这还有几周时间，所以你们现在有的是时间，通过发推把你们的诉求告诉 Anas。别发给我们，因为是 Anas 在收集这些信息。

turns.en: He's going to assimilate it, and we'll figure out what you guys want us to discuss in Anas' appearance in a Unplugged Session, which we'll do after a regular format.
turns.zh: 他会把这些内容消化吸收，然后我们就能搞清楚，你们希望大家在 Anas 上 Unplugged 专场时讨论些什么；那个专场我们会在常规节目之后做。

turns.en: Another thing I want to announce as I have this opportunity is we're definitely committed to keeping the flagship podcast interview length to a target of 45 to 55 minutes and not more.
turns.zh: 趁这个机会，我还想宣布另一件事：我们坚定承诺，把旗舰播客的访谈时长控制在45到55分钟这个目标区间，不会更长。

turns.en: That's out of respect for your time because we know you're busy. If you want the extended content, we'll always put it in a separate episode.
turns.zh: 这是出于对你们时间的尊重，因为我们知道你们很忙。如果你们想要更长的内容，我们永远会把它单独放到另一期节目里。

turns.en: So what you can expect when we bring Anas back is a fairly tight update on the market and what's going on in the Middle East, and then a much broader discussion in the follow-on, which will probably come a day later again.
turns.zh: 所以当我们把 Anas 请回来时，你们可以期待一场相当紧凑的市场以及中东局势最新进展，然后在随后那期——很可能又是隔天推出——展开一场范围广得多的讨论。

turns.en: But that one will be content that you've requested by tweeting it to Anas. Now let's dive into Rosie's latest interview, which covers secular inflation, why Rosie doesn't buy the popular narrative, the AI boom, and what could bust it?
turns.zh: 而那期的内容，正是你们通过给 Anas 发推点题要的。好，现在让我们进入 Rosie 的最新访谈，内容涵盖长期通胀（secular inflation）、Rosie 为什么不信那套流行叙事、AI 热潮，以及什么可能戳破它？

turns.en: Midterm elections is a setup for economic slowdown, as well as Washington gridlock, and much, much more. It's all coming up in today's episode of Macrovoices.
turns.zh: 中期选举会为经济放缓埋下伏笔，同时带来华盛顿的政治僵局，还有很多很多。这一切都会在今天这期 MacroVoices 里讲到。

turns.en: And I'm Patrick Suresna. Let's dive straight into this interview. Joining me now is David Rosenberg, also known as a best-selling author. New book coming out called Bear in the Bullring.
turns.zh: 我是 Patrick Ceresna。让我们直接进入这场访谈。现在加入我的是 David Rosenberg，他同时也是一位畅销书作者。新书即将出版，叫《Bear in the Bullring》。

turns.en: That's October 6th, already available for pre-order on Amazon. New ETF, Rosie ETF, boy, perfectly named. We'll come back to the book and the ETF at the end of the interview.
turns.zh: 那本书10月6日出版，现在已经可以在 Amazon 上预购。还有一只新 ETF，Rosie ETF，天，这名字起得太贴切了。我们会在访谈结束时再回来聊这本书和这只 ETF。

turns.en: David, I wanted to get you back on the program for one specific reason, which is it's hard to find anybody that is not flipped to inflationist, and maybe even inflation alarmist, because well, it's in vogue right now.
turns.zh: David，我想再把你请回节目，是有一个特别的原因：现在几乎所有人都倒向了通胀论者（inflationist），甚至可能是通胀恐慌论者（inflation alarmist），就因为这在当下很时髦，很难找到一个不随大流的人。

turns.en: Does anyone I know in this industry I can count on not to be an inflationist just because it's in vogue? It's David Rosenberg. So is inflation the thing we need to focus on, and if not, why not?
turns.zh: 在这个行业里，我认识的人当中，有谁能让我指望他不会仅仅因为通胀论时髦就变成通胀论者？那就是 David Rosenberg。所以，通胀到底是不是我们需要聚焦的东西？如果不是，那又是为什么？

turns.en: I'm never going to say that we shouldn't be watching inflation, because that would be an irresponsible comment to make. But if you're going to ask me, is inflation the risk that the media and pundits on the business cable shows and Wall Street research reports, is inflation the big threat that it's made out to be?
turns.zh: 我永远不会说我们不该盯着通胀，因为那么讲是不负责任的。但如果你要问我，通胀是不是像媒体、财经有线节目上的评论员以及华尔街研报所渲染的那样，是被夸大的那个大威胁？

turns.en: In my opinion, it's not. And what I find interesting is that the same people now talking about inflation because of energy, and specifically crack spreads and diesel, were the same people that were yelling about inflation back in the spring, summer, and fall of last year because of the Trump tariffs.
turns.zh: 在我看来，它不是。而我觉得有意思的是，现在这批因为能源、尤其是裂解价差（crack spreads）和柴油而大谈通胀的人，正是去年春天、夏天和秋天因为 Trump 关税而嚷嚷通胀的那批人。

turns.en: And we were going to have a mountain of product inflation, imported inflation. And you know what? That never really did happen. It's not as if we didn't get a temporary bump in inflation from the tariffs, but you really have to strain your eye to see it.
turns.zh: 他们当时说我们会有一大堆商品通胀、进口通胀。结果呢？那件事其实从没真正发生。倒不是说关税没带来一波短暂的通胀小抬升，但你真得费很大的劲才能看出来。

turns.en: And if it was going to show up in any persistent way, it would show up in the core goods CPI index. And what's interesting is that a year ago, the year of your trend in the core goods CPI was running at one and a half percent.
turns.zh: 如果它要以任何持续的方式显现出来，那它会体现在核心商品 CPI 指数上。有意思的是，一年前，核心商品 CPI 的同比趋势还在1.5%的水平。

turns.en: Today it's running below 0.7 percent. It's at a four year low. So I would just ask the question, if we didn't get the big inflation from the big tariffs, and when you look at what the net effective tariff rate did, I mean, it went up a whole lot and the biggest increase since the early to mid 1930s, but there was never a sustained pass through the final inflation where you think it would hit the most, which was in
turns.zh: 今天它已经跌到0.7%以下，处在四年低点。所以我只想问一句：既然我们从这么大的关税里都没得到大通胀——而当你看净有效关税率（net effective tariff rate）的走势，它涨了一大截，是1930年代初到中期以来的最大升幅——但从没有出现过持续传导到最终通胀的情况，而你以为它最可能砸中的地方，恰恰是

turns.en: the core product sector. And in fact, it's been decelerating over the past year. Somebody must have eaten the tariff increase. Was it the exporter who didn't want a sacrifice market share?
turns.zh: 核心商品部门。而事实上，它在过去一年里一直在减速。总得有人把这波关税涨幅吃掉。是不想牺牲市场份额的出口商吗？

turns.en: Was it the importer at the border? Did it show up in profit margins in the affected sectors along the way? Or maybe all three, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating.
turns.zh: 是边境上的进口商吗？它有没有沿途体现在受影响行业的利润率里？又或者三者都有。但归根结底，事实胜于雄辩。

turns.en: And I asked the question and we could extend the conversation further, but I would ask the people that think that because of a one trick pony, which was, which is energy, why will that cause the sustained inflation that the Trump tariffs have managed to do?
turns.zh: 我提出这个问题，我们当然可以把话题再往下延伸，但我想问那些认为仅仅因为能源这匹只有一招的独角戏就会引发通胀的人：凭什么能源会造成那种持续通胀，而 Trump 关税都未能做到？

turns.en: Well, you make an excellent point. And I think it's also echoed. I had Harley Bassman on a couple of weeks ago, he says, boy, the inflation narrative sure does sound good, easy to talk to, but the data says it's not happening.
turns.zh: 嗯，你说得非常好。我觉得这也得到了印证。我几周前请了 Harley Bassman 上节目，他说，天，这套通胀叙事听起来确实好听、好聊，但数据说明它并没有发生。

turns.en: And he had a couple of slides up talking about, you know, what's going on with break evens and CPI and so forth and said that the numbers just don't support this narrative.
turns.zh: 他还放了几张幻灯片，讲盈亏平衡通胀率（breakevens）和 CPI 等的走势，说这些数据根本支撑不起这套叙事。

turns.en: And so that definitely confirms what you're saying, but here's why I'm a little bit stuck on this. I think the people that are worried about crude oil prices spiking, you know, that's probably going to be shorter term.
turns.zh: 所以这确实印证了你的说法。但我之所以还有点卡在这儿，是这个原因：我觉得那些担心原油价格飙升的人，那大概会是短期的。

turns.en: But what we need is finished products. And when they blow refineries up, a lot of them around the world, we didn't have enough of those already, and they don't come back when the war ends.
turns.zh: 但我们需要的是成品油。当他们把炼油厂炸掉——世界各地有很多炼油厂——我们本来就不够用了，而且这些东西并不会在战争结束后就恢复。

turns.en: It takes years to rebuild that stuff. So what I see as a potential inflation driver, and I don't know how it gets balanced out against other stuff, is if you keep blowing refineries up and you can't make the diesel fuel out of the crude oil, you end up with plenty of crude oil and no diesel fuel.
turns.zh: 重建那些设施要好几年。所以我视为一个潜在通胀推手的东西——我也不知道它怎么和其他因素相互抵消——就是如果你不停地炸炼油厂，又没法把原油炼成柴油，你最后就会有一大堆原油、却没有柴油。

turns.en: Is that a potential inflation risk that we wouldn't be able to mitigate? I see that as a risk as to why we're not going to get a whole lot of price relief.
turns.zh: 那会不会是一个我们没法缓解的潜在通胀风险？我把这视为一个风险，正是它导致我们不会得到多少价格上的缓解。

turns.en: So this won't be a case like you had, for example, in Gulf War I, I mean, I have to go all the way back to 1990 when probably most of the listeners were in great school, you know, and you went from 20 to 40 on WTI and then quickly reversed right back to 20.
turns.zh: 所以这不会像你举的例子那样，比如海湾战争第一次——我是说，我得一路回到1990年，那时候大概大多数听众还在念书——WTI 从20美元冲到40美元，然后又迅速跌回20美元。

turns.en: What's the war ended? So I would say that, no, I don't think that your thesis leads to continuously higher refined product increases in energy.
turns.zh: 战争一结束就跌回去了？所以我会说，不，我不认为你的推断会导致成品油和能源价格持续走高。

turns.en: I think that we'll just stay at an elevated level. And the reality is that even though the conflict is ongoing between the US and Iran, we are seeing traffic flow through Hormuz that we haven't seen since the beginning of the war, and we're seeing exports in the Gulf region starting to be ramped up pretty significantly, especially in that very critical Saudi Arabia east-west pipeline.
turns.zh: 我认为它们只会停留在一个偏高的水平。而现实是，尽管美国和伊朗之间的冲突还在持续，我们却看到通过霍尔木兹（Hormuz）的运输流量恢复到开战以来没见过的程度，海湾地区的出口也开始相当显著地回升，尤其是那条极其关键的 Saudi Arabia 东西向管道。

turns.en: So I think that the relief won't come from prices coming down significantly, they'll stay elevated, but remember that inflation is not a level.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，缓解不会来自价格大幅回落——它们会维持在高位；但要记住，通胀不是一个水平值。

turns.en: Inflation has a rate of change. So even if diesel stays where it is, if gasoline prices stay where they are, maybe they come down a little bit, in 12 months time, it still falls out of the data.
turns.zh: 通胀是一个变化率。所以即便柴油停在原位、汽油价格停在原位，也许还略降一点，12个月之后，它照样会从数据里滚落出去。

turns.en: You're not going to get as big of a push down in inflation as you would obviously arithmetically if energy prices, you know, were to even reverse half of the big run up.
turns.zh: 你不会得到那么大的通胀下行推力——从算术上讲，如果能源价格哪怕回吐这波大涨的一半，你本该得到那么大的推力。

turns.en: But all you need to have the momentum stop is to just have energy prices peak out, which is what I think is going to happen. The other part of it is how we want to look at inflation, because it's not really a moment in time.
turns.zh: 但你只需要能源价格见顶，就能让这股势头停下来，而我认为这正是将会发生的。另一部分是关于我们想怎么看通胀，因为它其实并不是某一个时间点上的事。

turns.en: The problem is that, you know, we live in the here and now, we're inundated with news, social media, we have our Bloomberg terminals, we could see the tickers every second, but inflation is a process.
turns.zh: 问题在于，我们活在当下，被新闻、社交媒体淹没，我们有自己的 Bloomberg 终端，每一秒都能盯着行情跳动，但通胀是一个过程。

turns.en: Now the reason why we had 18 months of non-transitory inflation in, say, 2021, 2022, in a 2023 is because it did feed into wages. That is necessary for this to become truly a sustained inflationary development, as opposed to just a shock that lasts a few months.
turns.zh: 我们在2021、2022和2023那大约18个月里之所以出现非短暂性（non-transitory）通胀，正是因为它传导进了工资。要让这真正成为一场持续性的通胀演变、而不只是一场持续几个月的冲击，这一步是必需的。

turns.en: Now the reason we had the wage price spiral in the last 18 months, it really wasn't transitory when all was said and done, but then again, it wasn't the 1970s either.
turns.zh: 而在过去那18个月里，我们之所以出现工资—物价螺旋（wage price spiral），说到底它真的不是短暂性的，但话又说回来，那也不是1970年代。

turns.en: You remember the 1970s, we had repeated oil shocks, but the economy was unionized and everybody had a cola clause. So the labor market had bargaining power.
turns.zh: 你还记得1970年代，我们有一轮又一轮的石油冲击，但当时经济是高度工会化的，人人都有生活成本调整条款（COLA clause）。所以劳动力市场有议价能力。

turns.en: Now for a period coming out of COVID, because the government, through its endless stupidity, not just decided to give people $2 trillion of stimulus checks to spend just as the economy reopened.
turns.zh: 而在疫情后的一段时间里，之所以会这样，是因为政府凭着它没完没了的蠢操作，不只是决定在经济重开之际给人们发2万亿美元的刺激支票去花。

turns.en: But the government was paying people not to work for two years and paying them more. So then the business sector, when the economy reopened, had to pay up even more to attract labor back into the market.
turns.zh: 而且政府还连续两年付钱让人们不去工作，还付得更多。于是当经济重开时，企业部门不得不付出更高的价钱，才能把劳动力重新吸引回市场。

turns.en: So you had this wage price spiral. This is what's critical. Prices have to feed in the wages. Because if the price shock doesn't feed in the wages, it hits the wall in the labor market.
turns.zh: 所以你就有了这场工资—物价螺旋。这才是关键：价格必须传导进工资。因为如果价格冲击没有传导进工资，它就会在劳动力市场这堵墙上撞停。

turns.en: And all you end up with is negative real wages that then trigger an environment of negative real consumer demand, which means that, yes, you will get inflation in, say, fuels and possibly in the food as well when you look at fertilizer and the wholesale market for grains.
turns.zh: 你最终得到的，只是转负的实际工资，进而触发一个实际消费需求转负的环境。这意味着，是的，你会在燃料上看到通胀，可能还有食品——当你看化肥以及谷物的批发市场时。

turns.en: Yes, that's true. There's stuff. We still have to fill our cars and we still have to eat. But the other, call it 80, 85% of the pricing pie ends up coming under downward pressure because you get demand destruction in the more cyclical parts of the economy.
turns.zh: 是的，那是真的。有些东西我们躲不掉：我们还是得给车加油，还是得吃饭。但另外那大约80%到85%的价格盘子，最终会承受下行压力，因为你会在经济中更具周期性的那些部分出现需求破坏。

turns.en: In services and goods. So the stuff that you don't need, the discretionary stuff, those prices come under downward pressure. So it's a relative price game for it to become sustained inflation for us to be worried about.
turns.zh: 无论是服务还是商品。所以那些你不需要的、可选消费的东西，那些价格会承受下行压力。因此这是一场相对价格的博弈；要让它变成那种值得我们担心的持续性通胀，

turns.en: You have to see it and turn it into the labor market and we're not seeing it right now. And it's very interesting for anybody that wants to see a Fed official that may be pushing against Kevin Warsh, who says wages don't matter.
turns.zh: 你必须看到它传导进劳动力市场并在那里转向，而我们现在并没有看到。而对于任何想看一位可能在顶着 Kevin Warsh 的美联储官员——Warsh 说工资不重要——的人来说，很有意思的是，

turns.en: John Williams of the New York Fed just gave a speech on September 29th, talking about we see no evidence that these price shocks are entering into wages.
turns.zh: 纽约联储的 John Williams 刚在9月29日做了一场讲话，说我们没有看到任何证据表明这些价格冲击正在进入工资。

turns.en: Therefore, the inflation situation is unlikely to become self-reinforcing. Now, people say, well, Williams was part of the transitory crowd.
turns.zh: 因此，通胀局势不太可能变得自我强化。当然，有人会说，Williams 本来就是短暂论（transitory）那一拨的。

turns.en: The thing is that where he got it wrong was that it fed into wages. So it was a different labor market. The labor market was heating up dramatically coming out of COVID.
turns.zh: 问题在于，他当初判断错的地方，是通胀传导进了工资。所以那是一个不同的劳动力市场。疫情后劳动力市场在急剧升温。

turns.en: The quits rate was surging. The hiring rate was surging. The job opening rate was surging. Labor demand was out of control. We don't have that environment today.
turns.zh: 辞职率在飙升，招聘率在飙升，职位空缺率在飙升。劳动力需求失控。我们今天没有那样的环境。

turns.en: And in fact, in normal terms, wages are decelerating. So to me, that is going to be the catalyst for whether this turns into something more sinister than just an energy price shock.
turns.zh: 而事实上，用正常口径看，工资增速正在放缓。所以对我来说，那将成为判断这件事会不会演变成比一场能源价格冲击更凶险的东西的催化剂。

turns.en: Because if the labor market is not strong enough to cause wages to play catch up and it's not happening, then all this ends up being is almost the same thing as a tax shock.
turns.zh: 因为如果劳动力市场不够强，不足以推动工资去追赶物价——而它现在并没有——那么这一切最终几乎就等同于一场税收冲击。

turns.en: It's really akin to a tax increase. Would you consider a tax increase to be inflationary? Well, it would be if you go to your boss and used to, hey, my taxes went up.
turns.zh: 它真的很像一次加税。你会认为加税是通胀性的吗？嗯，如果你去找老板说，嘿，我的税涨了，

turns.en: I want higher wages. But this is a tax increase. And it is not sustainable unless the labor market plays ball. And that was the missing link last year.
turns.zh: 我要更高的工资，那它就会是。但这其实是一次加税。而且除非劳动力市场配合，否则它是不可持续的。而这就是去年缺失的那一环。

turns.en: We don't have to go back five, 10 years. We had the tariff shock. Where was the inflation? Where was the inflation from the tariff shock? It was small and now it's totally reversed.
turns.zh: 我们不必回到五年、十年前。我们就经历了关税冲击。那场关税冲击带来的通胀在哪儿？它很小，而且现在完全反转了。

turns.en: It's faded into the review mirror. Why? Because it didn't filter into wages. That's the key. Besides the fact that we could sit here and talk all day long about diesel, the filter through to transportation, freight.
turns.zh: 它已经消散在后视镜里了。为什么？因为它没有渗进工资。这才是关键。更不用说，我们本可以整天坐在这儿聊柴油，聊它向运输、货运的传导。

turns.en: That's about a 5% inflation impulse. I mean, because forecasting inflation, it is a complex process. Labor is 30%, 30% of the cost at the retail level.
turns.zh: 那大约是5%的通胀脉冲。我是说，因为预测通胀是一个复杂的过程。劳动力占零售层面成本的30%。

turns.en: It's six times more powerful than energy. But we don't see labor costs minute by minute on our Bloomberg screen. We see what energy is doing.
turns.zh: 它的影响力是能源的六倍。但我们在 Bloomberg 屏幕上并不是每分钟都能看到劳动力成本，我们看到的是能源在怎么走。

turns.en: So I will say that I will reserve my judgment until I see evidence that we're seeing bargaining agreements, collective bargaining agreements start to escalate.
turns.zh: 所以我会说，我会保留我的判断，直到我看到证据表明集体议价协议（collective bargaining agreements）开始升级。

turns.en: We start to see wage trends escalate. We'll see non-farm payrolls. I think average early earnings will be the most important number. Until that happens, until I see the labor market respond, I'll take the other side of the bet that this is going to be a major sustainable inflationary problem for the economy.
turns.zh: 直到我们看到工资趋势开始升级。我们会盯非农就业（non-farm payrolls）；我认为平均时薪（average hourly earnings）会是最重要的那个数字。在那之前，在我看到劳动力市场做出反应之前，我会站在赌局的另一边——我不认为这会成为一个重大的、可持续的通胀问题困扰经济。

turns.en: I saw another quote go by my screen that I'm pretty sure was attributed to you that I thought was really insightful, which is everybody's talking about, but the 10-year yield, and I think it was you who said, the rise in yields is 90% real rates and only 10% inflation expectations.
turns.zh: 我看到屏幕上又飘过一句话，我相当确定是归在你名下的，我觉得非常有洞见，就是当所有人都在谈10年期收益率时，我想是你说的：收益率的上升里，90%是实际利率（real rates），只有10%是通胀预期。

turns.en: I thought that was a brilliant quote, but okay, let's go to the next level. Why are we seeing right now such strength in real rates? Well, we have two things going on.
turns.zh: 我觉得那句话太精辟了。但好，我们进入下一个层次：为什么我们现在看到实际利率如此强劲？嗯，我们有两件事在同时发生。

turns.en: The first, of course, is the fact that we have these hyperscalers dramatically increasing their cat-backs commitments. And now three of the biggest of the four are now net-free cash flow negatives.
turns.zh: 第一件，当然是这些超大型云计算公司（hyperscalers）在大幅加码它们的资本支出（capex）承诺。如今四大里最大的三家，净自由现金流转负了。

turns.en: So they're going to the bond market and they're going to the long out of the bond market and the multiple currencies to fund their cat-backs boom.
turns.zh: 所以它们转向债券市场，而且是从债券市场的长端、以多种货币去融资，来支撑它们的资本支出热潮。

turns.en: So what's changed is that this is no longer being funded out of their cash flows. So now you're having corporate credit demands bumping against government credit demands, and that's one of the reasons why the real rate's gone up is because the demand for capital is going up.
turns.zh: 所以变化在于，这已经不再是用它们自己的现金流来融资了。于是你现在有了企业信用需求和政府信用需求相互顶牛，这正是实际利率上行的原因之一，因为对资本的需求在上升。

turns.en: People like to point to $40 trillion of government debt, with all due respect. When the 10-year treasury note yield was last below 4% in February, the national debt was $39 trillion.
turns.zh: 人们喜欢拿40万亿美元的政府债务说事。恕我直言，上一次10年期国债收益率低于4%是在2月，那时国债规模是39万亿美元。

turns.en: Now we're at 40. So this last trillion is we have a debt crisis on our hands. So we went from $38 trillion to $39 trillion from last October to this February.
turns.zh: 现在我们是40万亿。所以这最后的1万亿，就成了我们手上有一场债务危机。我们从去年10月到今年2月，从38万亿走到了39万亿。

turns.en: And nobody talked about that in the 10-year note yield went below 4% after adding a trillion dollars of debt from October 2025 to February 2026.
turns.zh: 而没有人谈论那件事；在2025年10月到2026年2月间增加了1万亿美元债务之后，10年期国债收益率还跌破了4%。

turns.en: At $39 trillion, nobody was talking about it. But now at 40, because it's a zero, everybody's talking about it. Because what people do, and I imagine they do this on your show and I see them do it on CNBC and Fox Business and on Bloomberg TV.
turns.zh: 在39万亿的时候，没人在谈它。但现在到了40万亿，因为多了个零，人人都在谈它。因为人们做的事——我猜在你们的节目上他们这么干，我在 CNBC、Fox Business 和 Bloomberg TV 上也看到他们这么干——

turns.en: What's been the biggest change? Because the AI spending boom was going on back in February when the 10-year note was below 4%. Government debt deficits, is that really new?
turns.zh: 最大的变化到底是什么？因为在2月10年期国债还低于4%的时候，AI 支出热潮就已经在进行了。政府债务、赤字，那真的是新鲜事吗？

turns.en: I started in the business in October 1987 when we always talked about where the twin deficits. Let's focus on what is the elephant in the room.
turns.zh: 我是1987年10月入行的，那时候我们总在谈双赤字（twin deficits）在哪儿。让我们聚焦于房间里那头真正的大象吧。

turns.en: What's changed the most is we have regime change at the Fed. So let me be emphatic and I can't prove it. It's just an opinion that if Powell were still in charge, most of this, I'm not going to say all of it, most of this would not be happening.
turns.zh: 变化最大的是，我们在美联储出现了政权更迭（regime change）。所以让我把话说重一点，而且我证明不了，这只是一个观点：如果 Powell 还在掌权，这里面的大部分——我不说全部——大部分都不会发生。

turns.en: I can't say all of it because when worst took over in June, the 10-year note was barely around 4.4 and we're up about 90 basis points since.
turns.zh: 我不能说全部，因为当 Warsh 在6月接手时，10年期国债才勉强在4.4%附近，而自那以后我们已经上行了大约90个基点（basis points）。

turns.en: But I think Powell carried through a different monetary policy. Powell never said, I'm focused on headline inflation. To most central bankers, it's always been core.
turns.zh: 但我认为 Powell 贯彻的是一种不同的货币政策。Powell 从没说过他盯着整体通胀（headline inflation）。对大多数央行行长来说，看的一直是核心通胀。

turns.en: Warsh his headline. And his new framework, which isn't even a framework, I don't know what to call it, but everybody's latched onto it, is the share of the PC deflator that's rising more than a 3% annual rate.
turns.zh: 而 Warsh 看的是整体通胀。他的新框架——那甚至算不上一个框架，我都不知道该怎么称呼它，但所有人都揪住了它——就是 PCE 平减指数里年率涨幅超过3%的那部分占比。

turns.en: As if that's a meaningful statistic. So basically, so what if a bag of peanuts is going up 10% and auto prices are going down 5% in his statistics, they're both equal.
turns.zh: 仿佛那是一个有意义的统计量似的。所以基本上，那又怎样？在他的统计里，一袋花生涨10%和汽车价格跌5%，两者是等价的。

turns.en: Bag of peanuts to Kevin Warsh is equivalent to an automobile. Think about how insane that is. And he's not giving guidance. He's really not giving much of a framework.
turns.zh: 对 Kevin Warsh 来说，一袋花生等同于一辆汽车。想想这有多荒唐。而且他并不给指引，他其实没给出多少框架。

turns.en: He has sounded hawkish. But then when he was vying for the job, he was dovish. Interesting that when he was applying to be Fed chairman, he was open about his favorite inflation statistic, which was the Dallas Fed trimming inflation measure, which last I saw was 2.3%.
turns.zh: 他一直 sounding 得很鹰派。但当初他竞聘这个职位时，他是偏鸽的。有意思的是，当他申请出任美联储主席时，他很坦率地讲过他最喜欢的通胀指标，那就是达拉斯联储的修剪均值通胀（Dallas Fed trimmed mean inflation），我最后一次看到时是2.3%。

turns.en: 30 basis points above the beloved and badly who 2% target. Wow, that's really a big deal. He doesn't talk about that anymore. So he's been tight leapt, but that means his words carry more weight.
turns.zh: 比那个备受珍爱、又被 badly 拿捏的2%目标高出30个基点。哇，那真是个了不起的大事。他现在不再谈那个了。所以他一直守口如瓶，但那意味着他的话分量更重。

turns.en: And he has come across as being very hawkish. And he managed to cobble together a consensus. The hike rates at the last meeting. Now, remember that back in February, the markets are priced for one or two rate cuts.
turns.zh: 而他给人的印象是非常鹰派。他还设法拼凑出了一个共识——上次会议加了息。现在记住，回到2月，市场当时定价的是一到两次降息。

turns.en: And then the Fed switches to a tightening bias, then they raise rates, and now the markets are priced for three or four more tightings on top of what they already did.
turns.zh: 然后美联储转向了紧缩倾向，接着他们加息，而现在市场定价的是在他们已经做的基础上还要再紧缩三到四次。

turns.en: So when you look at the arithmetic, how did we go up well over 100 basis points across a tertiary curve is because the market has reset from an accommodate of Fed to a tighter Fed.
turns.zh: 所以当你看这些算术：我们凭什么在整条收益率曲线上上行了远超100个基点？就是因为市场已经从一个宽松的美联储，重新定价为一个更紧的美联储。

turns.en: The Fed has taken the cost to carry away. Where are you going to hide? Well, you're going to hide at the front end of the curve, or you're going to go to the treasury bills.
turns.zh: 美联储把持有成本（cost to carry）拿走了。你要往哪儿躲？嗯，你会躲到曲线的前端，或者你会去买国库券（treasury bills）。

turns.en: Why would you want to take on duration with such a flat yield curve? So that's really what the story is. What has been the biggest change? The biggest change has been the reset of Fed expectations.
turns.zh: 在收益率曲线这么平的情况下，谁会愿意去承担久期（duration）呢？所以这才是真正的故事所在。最大的变化是什么？最大的变化就是美联储预期的重定价。

turns.en: That explains most of the run-up in yields we've had from the lows in late February, and has explained almost all of the increase we've had since Warsh took over back in the middle of June.
turns.zh: 这解释了我们从2月底低点以来收益率上行的大部分，也解释了自 Warsh 在6月中接手以来我们几乎所有的升幅。

turns.en: I think you hit the nail on the head with the phrase regime change at the Fed. I think that's exactly it. And I think it's even bigger than that.
turns.zh: 我觉得你用美联储政权更迭（regime change）这个说法一针见血。我认为正是如此。而且我觉得它比这还要更大。

turns.en: What I would say is it seems like between Warsh and Besant and the Trump administration, they've got an agenda to basically say we're going to take both monetary and fiscal policy in a different direction than it's been taken before.
turns.zh: 我想说的是，看起来在 Warsh、Bessent 和 Trump 政府之间，他们有一个议程，基本上就是要说：我们要把货币政策和财政政策都带向一个和以往不同的方向。

turns.en: We're going to do this differently. We've got our own plan. I can't figure out exactly what that plan is. It feels to me like there is a grand plan, though, that's bigger than just Fed FOMC policy.
turns.zh: 我们要用不同的方式来干这件事，我们有自己的计划。我没法确切搞清楚那个计划是什么。但对我来说，感觉确实是有一个宏大计划的，而且它比单纯的美联储 FOMC 政策要大。

turns.en: Do you agree with that? And if so, can you figure out what the big plan is? No, I can't figure it out. I can't figure out anything coming to Washington.
turns.zh: 你同意这个看法吗？如果同意，你能搞清楚那个大计划是什么吗？不，我搞不清楚。凡是 Washington 出来的东西我都搞不清楚。

turns.en: And there's no doubt that Warsh has done a giant pivot. He was not talking about, when he was appointed for the job, he wasn't lamenting about the fact that inflation has been above target for five years.
turns.zh: 毫无疑问，Warsh 完成了一次巨大的转向。当年他竞聘这个职位时，他可没在为通胀已经连续五年高于目标而 lamenting。

turns.en: But now he's in control of the Fed and his character has changed. Now, he's got a lot of support. In some sense, he's following the historical script because, you know, if you go all the way back to all the rookie Fed chairpeople, I say chairpeople because Jenny Yellen is a woman, but all the way back to Miller in the 70s, the first move by the rookie Fed chairperson was to raise rates at the first opportunity.
turns.zh: 但现在他掌控了美联储，他的性格变了。当然，他有很多支持。某种意义上，他在照着历史剧本走，因为如果你一路回溯所有那些新手美联储主席——我说 chairperson 是因为 Janet Yellen 是女性——但一直回到70年代的 Miller，新手美联储主席的第一个动作，都是在最早的时机加息。

turns.en: Remember I mentioned Greenspan when I started in the business, and he was raising rates pretty aggressively. Well, we know what happened next.
turns.zh: 记得我提到我入行时的 Greenspan 吗，他当时在相当激进地加息。嗯，接下来发生了什么我们都清楚。

turns.en: On the day I started in October 19th of 87, but the last Fed chairman to cut rates at the first meeting was Arthur Burns in 1970, and that's because the U.S. economy was entering into a recession.
turns.zh: 就在我入行那天，1987年10月19日。而最后一位在首次会议上就降息的美联储主席，是1970年的 Arthur Burns，那是因为当时美国经济正步入一场衰退。

turns.en: So that's the first thing. It's just a pattern. The first thing the Fed chairperson does, and Jenny Yellen, who people thought was a puffball, her first move was to hike rates in December 2015.
turns.zh: 所以这首先就是一个模式，是美联储主席上台做的第一件事。而 Janet Yellen——人们以为她是个软柿子——她的第一个动作就是在2015年12月加息。

turns.en: You're a Democrat, a labor market expert, historically a dove, raised rates at her first opportunity, and so he just fit the historical bill.
turns.zh: 她是民主党人、劳动力市场专家、一贯偏鸽，却在第一个机会就加了息，所以他只是完全符合了那个历史套路。

turns.en: I guess the central bankers feel they have to flex their inflation credentials right away. So maybe that's part of it. I don't like the fact that he really has not unveiled a framework as to what's going on.
turns.zh: 我猜央行官员们觉得必须马上亮出自己抗通胀的 credentials，所以也许这也是原因之一。我不喜欢的是，他其实没有拿出一个框架来说明到底怎么回事。

turns.en: He doesn't want to do that. He wants to leave all the guesswork up to the market, and so the market is reading every syllable as hawkish. I mean, if you noticed, whenever Warsh opens his mouth, the 10-year yield goes up such or seven basis points.
turns.zh: 他不想那么做。他想把所有的猜测都留给市场，所以市场在把他说的每一个音节都读成鹰派。我是说，如果你注意到，每当 Warsh 一开口，10年期收益率就上行个七八个基点。

turns.en: It's incredible. So they're interpreting whatever it is he's saying, and he's not saying much as being hawkish. Now, it is interesting that Williams looked like he pushed back a little bit on that in the September 29th speech, but we'll see what happens.
turns.zh: 这真是不可思议。所以他们在解读他说的任何东西——而他其实没说什么——把它当成鹰派。有意思的是，Williams 在9月29日那场讲话里看起来对这一点稍微顶了一下，但我们且看接下来会怎样。

turns.en: But I think that Fed policy, and it's amazing to me that everybody's coming out thinking that Warsh is great, and this is just a great Fed, and they're going to crush inflation.
turns.zh: 但我认为，美联储政策——让我吃惊的是，所有人都出来说 Warsh 很棒，说这是一个了不起的美联储，说他们将会碾压通胀。

turns.en: Everybody thinks inflation is a big problem, and everybody is begging. They're begging the Fed to raise rates. You have almost a record level.
turns.zh: 每个人都认为通胀是个大问题，每个人都在央求——他们在央求美联储加息。你几乎到了创纪录的水平。

turns.en: You said before, a record level of net spectrum of short positions on the CBOT when it comes to the 10-year note, it is sexy and fashionable to hate the bond market right now.
turns.zh: 你刚才说过，在 CBOT 上，就10年期国债而言，净投机空头（net speculative short）仓位处在创纪录水平。眼下做空债券市场是很性感、很时髦的事。

turns.en: You're viewed as a hero, the so-called bond vigilantes. Well, they're not really bond vigilantes. They're just basically looking at how the Fed is going to be influencing the cost to carry in the Treasury market, and the same Treasury market, those pricing in a couple of rate cuts six months ago, we're now pricing in four more rate hikes, and we'll see how that changes.
turns.zh: 你会被视为英雄，也就是所谓的债券义警（bond vigilantes）。嗯，他们其实算不上真正的债券义警。他们基本上只是在盯着美联储将如何影响国债市场的持有成本；而同样是这个国债市场，六个月前还在定价几次降息，现在却在定价再加息四次，我们且看这会怎么变。

turns.en: But no, Fed policy has me confused, and the administration's policy has me confused, totally confused. I mean, how can you go on to an affordability program ahead of the midterms, and then you want to engage in a trade war with your principal trading partner north of the border?
turns.zh: 但不，美联储政策让我困惑，政府的政策也让我困惑，彻底困惑。我是说，你怎么能一边在中期选举前推一个可负担性（affordability）方案，一边又想和你北部边境那个最主要的贸易伙伴打一场贸易战？

turns.en: How does that make any sense? And offering $5,000 as a dividend to voting citizens if the House and the Senate stay Republican, that's a trillion dollars.
turns.zh: 这怎么讲得通？还有，如果众议院和参议院都留在共和党手里，就给投票的公民派发5,000美元的红利——那可是1万亿美元。

turns.en: How does that solve inflation? That sort of giveaway was one of the reasons we had inflation. The Biden followed by Trump giveaway, the $2 trillion fiscal stimulus checks, that accounted for more than half the inflation we saw going from zero to 9% from, let's say, call 2020 to 2022.
turns.zh: 那怎么可能解决通胀？那种撒钱恰恰是我们当初出现通胀的原因之一。Biden 接着 Trump 的撒钱，那2万亿美元的财政刺激支票，占了我们从0冲到9%那波通胀的一半以上——就算是从2020年到2022年吧。

turns.en: So there's not much I can say that I fully comprehend. Besson says, I'm the House. You want to bet against the House? Bet against the House?
turns.zh: 所以能说我完全理解的东西不多。Bessent 说，我就是庄家。你想和庄家对赌？和庄家对赌？

turns.en: Well, people are betting against the House. Maybe a comment he shouldn't have said doesn't show too much humility. But we'll see what happens after.
turns.zh: 嗯，人们就是在和庄家对赌。也许这是一句他本不该说的话，没表现出多少谦逊。但我们且看之后会怎样。

turns.en: There's two dates we should circle on the calendar. One is November 3rd. That's the midterms. And it looks as though the Democrats take the House.
turns.zh: 有两个日期我们该在日历上圈出来。一个是11月3日，那是中期选举。而且看起来民主党会拿下众议院。

turns.en: There's now, in the prediction polls, more than 50% chance they take the Senate. But if they take the House, that's what whoever meets the road for fiscal policy, because that's where the spending bills get passed.
turns.zh: 如今在预测民调里，他们拿下参议院的概率已经超过50%。但如果他们拿下众议院，那对财政政策来说就是撞上了一堵墙，因为支出法案是在众议院通过的。

turns.en: So we're going to get fiscal, we're going to get policy gridlock. What this is going to change after November 3rd is we're going to go into a period of gridlock.
turns.zh: 所以我们会得到财政上的、政策上的僵局。11月3日之后将会改变的，是我们要进入一段僵持期。

turns.en: And people always said on the bond market, gridlock is good because the executive branch and the legislative branch typically are at odds with each other and nothing gets done.
turns.zh: 而人们在债市上总是说，僵局是好事，因为行政分支和立法分支通常相互对立，什么都做不成。

turns.en: And I say, if nothing gets done on fiscal policy, because look, one of the reasons why you could argue, the economy has done fairly well this year.
turns.zh: 而我要说，如果财政政策上什么都做不成——因为你看，今年经济之所以可以说表现还不错，原因之一是

turns.en: And it's been equity wealth effect on spending at the high end on luxury goods and services. It's been the AI spending boom, although a lot of that has been offset by rising imports.
turns.zh: 高端消费、奢侈品和服务上的股市财富效应；还有 AI 支出热潮，尽管其中很多被上升的进口抵消掉了。

turns.en: But the one big, beautiful bill, right? That never would have been passed had Trump not had Congress being dominated by the Republicans. And so it's amazing what you can accomplish when you have one party power.
turns.zh: 但那个 one big beautiful bill（大而美法案），对吧？如果 Trump 没有一个被共和党主导的国会，它根本不可能通过。所以当你有一党独大的权力时，你能办成的事是很惊人的。

turns.en: The one big, beautiful bill was huge stimulus for the economy this year. The depreciation allowance, the huge income tax refunds, you can't extrapolate that in the future.
turns.zh: 那个 one big beautiful bill 对今年的经济是巨大的刺激。折旧减免、大额的所得税退税——你没法把这个外推到未来。

turns.en: These were one-offs and they come to an end basically. There's no more fiscal stimulus in the economy after November 3rd. Have the bond bears factored that into their analysis.
turns.zh: 这些都是一次性的，而且它们基本上要走到头了。11月3日之后，经济里就没有更多财政刺激了。那些债券空头把这一点纳入他们的分析了吗？

turns.en: We will not realize that 80% of the time, historically, when a one-party power after a national election swings to a two-party system with gridlock, 80% of the time the economy slows, 80% of the time inflation goes down, and 80% of the time bond yields go down in that two-year period between the time of the midterms where you get the gridlock to the next election.
turns.zh: 我们不会意识到：从历史看，有80%的概率，当一党独大在一场全国性选举后转为两党分立、带僵局的格局时，80%的概率经济会放缓，80%的概率通胀会下行，80%的概率债券收益率会在从出现僵局的中期选举到下一次选举之间的那两年里走低。

turns.en: This will be in 2028. I'll take those 80% odds. And that's because we get the fiscal gridlock. The Democrats aren't going to work with Trump.
turns.zh: 这将是在2028年。我接受这80%的赔率。那是因为我们会有财政僵局。民主党不会和 Trump 合作。

turns.en: And even if Trump wants to work with the Democrats, he used to be a Democrat way back in the day. I can only talk about what I have confidence in.
turns.zh: 而即便 Trump 想和民主党合作——他早年很久以前可是个民主党人。我只能就我有把握的事情发表看法。

turns.en: I can only have confidence in the calendar, November 3rd's the midterms. I think we have a good idea how that's going to play out. And I think that's going to end this past six years of insane fiscal stimulus.
turns.zh: 我唯一能有把握的就是日历：11月3日是中期选举。我想我们对它会怎么走有一个不错的判断。而且我认为那会终结过去这六年疯狂的财政刺激。

turns.en: That's been great for the economy, but it has been, you could say, a source of inflation from an aggregate demand perspective, but it certainly has also been a positive for the stock market.
turns.zh: 那种刺激对经济是好事，但你也可以说，从总需求的角度看它是一个通胀来源；当然它对股市也一直是个利好。

turns.en: But that comes to an end. Then November 4th is the Treasury funding announcement. And I'm sort of thinking that if his buyback program got a lot of press, but I mean, whatever, $6 billion into a market that turns over by a trillion dollars a day is not going to have a big impact. But the Treasury does have a very big impact, not on the demand for fixed income assets.
turns.zh: 但那要走到头了。然后11月4日是财政部的再融资公告（Treasury funding announcement）。我有点在想，如果他的回购计划得到了很多关注，但我是说，管它呢，在一个每天换手1万亿美元的市场上投入60亿美元，是不会有什么大影响的。但财政部确实对债市有非常大的影响——不是对固收资产的需求。

turns.en: That's the Fed. The Fed could do that through its balance sheet. But the Treasury department has a huge influence on the supply. They are the suppliers of the debt.
turns.zh: 那是美联储的事。美联储可以通过它的资产负债表来做那件事。但财政部对供给有巨大的影响力。他们是债务的供给方。

turns.en: They can choose what maturities. And so I am thinking and answering the question about the bond market, what might happen that could come as a surprise is what happened back in early November of 2023.
turns.zh: 他们可以选择发行哪些期限。所以，在回答关于债市、可能出现什么意外的问题时，我在想的是2023年11月初发生过的事。

turns.en: When Janet Yellen was Treasury Secretary and the Treasury funding announcement, she dramatically cut the supply issuance of bonds and notes and flooded the market with bills.
turns.zh: 当时 Janet Yellen 是财政部长，在那份财政部再融资公告里，她大幅削减了债券和票据的供给发行，同时向市场大量投放国库券（bills）。

turns.en: And you had an enormous rally in the 10-year note. The 10-year note from late October to the end of December went down to under-basis points.
turns.zh: 然后你在10年期国债上看到了一轮巨大的反弹。10年期国债从10月底到12月底，收益率下行了数十个基点。

turns.en: Is anybody talking about that? Your first question to me was about diesel and about inflation and labor market. Nobody's talking about the Treasury funding on November 4th.
turns.zh: 有人在谈这个吗？你问我的第一个问题是关于柴油、关于通胀和劳动力市场的。没人在谈11月4日的财政部再融资。

turns.en: When I speak in front of group people and I ask them if they can tell me when November 4th is going to be why it's important, everybody says to me it's the midterm elections.
turns.zh: 当我在一群人面前讲话、问他们能不能告诉我11月4日为什么重要时，所有人都跟我说，那是中期选举。

turns.en: I say, no, that's the day before. November 4th is a Treasury funding announcement and that could be a very big deal. Just remember how powerful that influence was on the yield curve back in the fall of 2023.
turns.zh: 我说，不对，那是前一天。11月4日是财政部再融资公告，那可能是件非常大的事。只要回想一下2023年秋天那个公告对收益率曲线的影响力有多强就知道了。

turns.en: We may well see a repeat of that. So I'll reserve judgment about Besant, but I think that's what he's going to do. It's not really an operation twist.
turns.zh: 我们很可能看到那一幕重演。所以关于 Bessent 我会保留判断，但我认为那正是他会做的事。它其实不是一次扭曲操作（operation twist）。

turns.en: It's just influencing the shape of the curve by cutting back on long-dated issuance. And that's really where the big problem has been. And when you think about it, the economy is priced off the 10-year note.
turns.zh: 它只是通过削减长期债券的发行来影响曲线的形状。而那里恰恰才是大问题所在。而且你想想，整个经济是以10年期国债来定价的。

turns.en: Nothing else really matters as much. David, I couldn't possibly agree more. And I think what you've just said about the midterms is the insight that seems to be missing from the market.
turns.zh: 其他任何东西的重要性都比不上它。David，我再同意不过了。而且我认为你刚才说的关于中期选举的话，正是市场似乎缺失的那个洞见。

turns.en: We're pretty darn close to all-time highs here. There's not a whole lot of volatility in stocks as we're a month away from an election where the polling is telling us.
turns.zh: 我们现在离历史高点已经非常近了。股市里没有多少波动率，而我们距离一场选举只有一个月，民调正在告诉我们——

turns.en: And I'm not taking any side on who's right, left or right, who's wrong. That's not what Macrovoices is for. But if the polls are telling us that the political party that's impeached the current president twice before and doesn't like him is about to take at least one and maybe both houses of Congress, that seems like a pretty darn big risk factor that I would expect the market's fear of uncertainty to just be going on steroids right now.
turns.zh: 而且我不在任何一边站队，谁左谁右、谁对谁错，那不是 MacroVoices 的宗旨。但如果民调在告诉我们，那个曾经两次弹劾现任总统、而且不喜欢他的政党，即将拿下国会的至少一院、也许两院，那看起来就是一个相当大的风险因素，我本以为市场对不确定性的恐惧此刻应该像打了类固醇一样飙升。

turns.en: But it seems like nobody's really talking about it. I don't get it. I think as we're still fixated on what's happening with energy, we have a new Fed chairman.
turns.zh: 但似乎真的没人在谈它。我不明白。我想，当我们仍然死盯着能源上发生的事时，我们有了一位新的美联储主席。

turns.en: There's a debate as to just how strong the economy is. So there are so many moving pieces. But there is talk about the midterms. But they're in the marketplace, not a lot of talk about what are the implications of this political shift on the stock market and the bond market.
turns.zh: 关于经济到底有多强，也有一场辩论。所以有太多移动的部件。市场上确实有关于中期选举的讨论，但关于这场政治转向对股市和债市意味着什么，讨论并不多。

turns.en: Now, look, when you go back, for example, and this is why people get a little upset with me when I talk about politics, and I never really take sides.
turns.zh: 现在，你看，当你回溯——比方说，这也是为什么人们在我谈政治时会有点不爽，而我从不真正站队。

turns.en: I will be critical. I was as critical of Obama and Biden and Trump almost equally when I thought that it was necessary. But I'm more into trying to help people wait through how the politics can influence the financial markets.
turns.zh: 我会批评。当我觉得有必要时，我对 Obama、Biden 和 Trump 的批评几乎是一样多的。但我更投入的，是设法帮人们判断政治会如何影响金融市场。

turns.en: That's what consumes me. For example, when you go back to early November of 2024, the last election, did you see in the days and weeks after the election, the stock market surged, and the treasury market got spanked, spanked, like it is today, actually.
turns.zh: 那才是让我全神贯注的事。举个例子，当你回到2024年11月初，上一场大选，你有没有看到在选举后的那些天和几周里，股市大涨，而国债市场被痛打——被痛打，就像今天这样，其实。

turns.en: Today for a different reason. Back then, it's because not because Trump won the election. It's because it was a red wave. It was a clean sweep.
turns.zh: 今天是因为另一个原因。而当时，不是因为 Trump 赢了选举，而是因为那是一场红色浪潮（red wave），是一次全面横扫。

turns.en: The Republicans took the House, took the Senate, and yet Trump had power, and you knew at that point the one big beautiful bill was coming, and the bond market and the stock market acted accordingly.
turns.zh: 共和党拿下了众议院、拿下了参议院，Trump 掌握了一党权力，你在那一刻就知道 one big beautiful bill 要来了，债市和股市都相应地做出了反应。

turns.en: Stock surged on the implications for profits from depreciation allowances and income tax refunds, no tax on tips, all the stuff he campaigned on.
turns.zh: 股票大涨，是因为折旧减免和所得税退税对利润的影响，还有小费免税，所有他竞选时承诺的那些东西。

turns.en: That's really what was important about one-party sweep and bond yield soared. When you go back to when Trump won in November 2016, Trump won 0.0, and he campaigned on tax cuts, which he got through.
turns.zh: 那才是一党横扫真正重要的地方，而债券收益率飙升。当你回到 Trump 在2016年11月胜选时——他以减税为竞选主张，而且他把它推行了。

turns.en: Do you remember how the bond market puked in November 2016 election? Stock market surged after a pretty tough year. Then when you go to the midterms and you get the split government, not typically good news for equities, and bonds tend to like it because of the gridlock.
turns.zh: 你还记得2016年11月大选后债市是怎么剧烈下挫的吗？股市在经历了相当艰难的一年之后大涨。然后到了中期选举，你得到分裂政府（split government），那对股票通常不是好消息，而债券往往喜欢它，因为僵局。

turns.en: The same thing happened. You can go all the way back if you want to. Remember like yesterday when Clinton got elected in 1992, clean sweep, and people thought he was a borderline socialist.
turns.zh: 同样的事发生了。如果你愿意，你可以一路回溯。还记得就像昨天一样，Clinton 在1992年当选，全面横扫，当时人们以为他是个准社会主义者。

turns.en: Then look what happened when we had New Greengrinch contract with America and we went to split government in 1994 and we had the mother of all bond rallies.
turns.zh: 然后看看1994年，当我们有了 Newt Gingrich 的 Contract with America（与美国人民的契约）、转向分裂政府时发生了什么——我们迎来了所有债券反弹之母。

turns.en: So the politics matter. I agreed nobody's really talking about two dates. Now basically, I'm probably early like I usually am, but I've started to dip my toes into, I've already owned a lot of two-year notes because I don't think the Fed's going to be raising rates four times.
turns.zh: 所以政治是要紧的。我同意，其实没人在谈那两个日期。现在，基本上——我大概又抢跑了，像我平常一样——但我已经开始试探性地建仓了；我已经持有很多2年期国债，因为我不认为美联储会加息四次。

turns.en: They didn't even signal that, but the market thinks they did because there's really ineffective communication coming out of the Fed. The market thinks the Fed is going to, inflation is such a problem, the Fed's going to have to raise rates aggressively.
turns.zh: 他们甚至都没那样暗示过，但市场认为他们暗示了，因为美联储的沟通实际上很无效。市场认为美联储会——通胀是如此大的一个问题，美联储将不得不激进加息。

turns.en: I don't have that view, but the market's got that view. But I think that there's going to be two things. November 3rd, midterms, and people will realize that we've exiting finally the fiscal insanity.
turns.zh: 我不这么看，但市场是这么看的。但我认为会有两件事：11月3日，中期选举，人们会意识到我们终于走出了这种财政疯狂。

turns.en: Maybe we have to thank the Democrats. I mean, I see it both ways. I think that we just have moved to an economy and a financial market and a political spectrum that is just extreme, but the Republicans have not proven to have been good managers of fiscal policy.
turns.zh: 也许我们得感谢民主党。我是说，我两种看法都能看到。我觉得我们只是转到了一个极端的经济、极端的金融市场和极端的政治光谱，但共和党并没有证明自己是好的财政政策管理者。

turns.en: The good thing about split government is that nothing gets done and that's what we need to at least not have the deficit rise any further. And that also means that's going to have incrementally a depressing impact on the accurate demand because government's part of the economy.
turns.zh: 分裂政府的好处是什么都做不成，而这正是我们所需要的——至少能让赤字不再进一步上升。而这也意味着，它会对总需求产生一种增量式的抑制影响，因为政府是经济的一部分。

turns.en: So I think that's good news for those of us that want to see the economy cool off. I want to see bond yields come down because I'm one of the few that have not thrown in the towel.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，这对我们这些想看到经济降温的人是好消息。我想看到债券收益率回落，因为我是少数几个还没认输的人之一。

turns.en: And then November the 4th, the Treasury funding. And there's been three other times in the past where the Treasury did something like what Jenny Yellen did in 2023.
turns.zh: 然后11月4日，财政部再融资。过去还有另外三次，财政部做过类似 Janet Yellen 在2023年做的事。

turns.en: And you can shrug your shoulders and say, yeah, I don't really care. Well, let me tell you something. When people try and figure out what the hell happened in the fall of 2023, coming off the mother of all Fed tightening cycles, we had chat GPT.
turns.zh: 你可以耸耸肩说，是啊，我其实不在乎。嗯，让我告诉你一件事：当人们试图弄清2023年秋天到底发生了什么时——在史上最凶悍的美联储紧缩周期之后，我们有了 ChatGPT。

turns.en: At that point, the AI trade was taken off. Okay. This is the fall of 2023 out of the blue 100 basis point rally in a 10 year note and barely more than two months.
turns.zh: 在那个时点，AI 交易已经启动。好，这是2023年秋天，突然间10年期国债在仅仅两个多月的时间里反弹了100个基点。

turns.en: Why? Because of what the Treasury did at the refunding announcement. And of course, Jenny Yellen did that after a very pernicious increase in long-term rates.
turns.zh: 为什么？因为财政部在再融资公告时做的事。当然，Janet Yellen 是在长期利率出现了一轮非常有害的上升之后才那么做的。

turns.en: And it wasn't intervention. It was just a shift in emphasis on where they were going to issue across the curve. And I have a sense that if Besson wants to do anything along the same lines after a similar run-up in bond yields, he'll do something very similar.
turns.zh: 那不是干预。那只是在他们将沿曲线发行的各个期限上的一次侧重点转移。而我有一种感觉，如果 Bessent 想在债券收益率类似飙升之后做点沿着同样思路的事，他会做非常相似的事。

turns.en: It's much more powerful than what he's doing on the bond buybacks. That's really a drop in the bucket. What the Treasury can do on the supply side is where the power really comes in Scott Besson's office.
turns.zh: 这远比他在债券回购上做的那些事更有力量。那些回购其实只是沧海一粟。财政部在供给侧能做的事，才是力量真正所在——就藏在 Scott Bessent 的办公室里。

turns.en: I want to go back to something you mentioned earlier, which is the AI bubble. And obviously it's going strong. And I was really thinking it has to continue going strong because it's obviously the Trump administration's big priority is to focus on it.
turns.zh: 我想回到你早先提到的一件事，就是 AI 泡沫。显然它还在强势推进。我一直在想，它必须继续强势，因为显然 Trump 政府的重中之重就是聚焦它。

turns.en: It's kind of an arms race with China, I think, and I kind of thought it had to continue. But I had Matt Barry on recently who said, look, what people don't see coming is these Chinese open source. That's the free AI models, which means you've got to buy your own hardware to run it on.
turns.zh: 我觉得这在某种意义上是和中国的一场军备竞赛，我曾以为它势必得持续下去。但我最近请了 Matt Barry 上节目，他说，看，人们没预见到的，是这些中国的开源、也就是免费的 AI 模型，这意味着你得自己买硬件来运行它。

turns.en: But you can get something that's basically just as good as the best frontier models were three months ago, just a few months ago. You can get that for free open source, run it on your own hardware.
turns.zh: 但你能得到一个基本上和三四个月前最顶尖的前沿模型一样好的东西——就在几个月前的水平。你能免费得到那个开源模型，在自己的硬件上运行。

turns.en: And there's an extra advantage of running it on your own hardware, which means you're airgapping yourself from anthropic or open AI's cloud.
turns.zh: 而且在自己的硬件上运行还有一个额外好处，那就是你把自己和 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 的云做了 airgap（物理隔离）。

turns.en: So they're not using your proprietary data to train their next model. Matt thinks that could potentially result in a trend where a lot of people, particularly corporations that are sick of having their data mined, say, look, we're going to run on our own hardware.
turns.zh: 这样它们就不会拿你的专有数据去训练它们的下一代模型。Matt 认为，这可能会催生一股趋势：很多人，尤其是那些受够了自己数据被开采的公司，会说，看，我们要在自己的硬件上运行。

turns.en: We're not going to use any more open AI, any more anthropic. We're just going to use this free Chinese stuff. Boy, knock on effects from that in terms of the Trump administration policy.
turns.zh: 我们不再用 OpenAI、不再用 Anthropic，我们就用这些免费的中国货。天哪，这对 Trump 政府政策的连锁反应，

turns.en: I can't even imagine what would happen. Is that the risk, the AI bubble popping? Because maybe there's an alternative we don't realize. I think that it's a great point, otherwise known as global competition.
turns.zh: 我甚至没法想象会发生什么。那会不会就是 AI 泡沫破裂的风险？因为也许存在一个我们还没意识到的替代方案。我觉得这是个好观点，说白了就是全球竞争。

turns.en: And in the final analysis we are seeing in real time that there are no real barriers to entry. And one way that I think China will once again, as it's done in the past, exert itself as a source of global disinflation.
turns.zh: 归根结底，我们正在实时看到，其实并不存在真正的进入壁垒。而我认为，中国将再次——就像它过去做过的那样——成为一股全球反通胀（disinflation）的来源。

turns.en: And that's again why people are saying, well, look at what AI has done with memory chip prices, sources of inflation, semiconductors, so on and so forth.
turns.zh: 这也正是为什么人们在说，看 AI 对内存芯片价格做了什么——那些是通胀的来源，半导体，等等等等。

turns.en: When push comes to shove, and this is not even including the future productivity benefits, which will be disinflationary, but that's out in the future.
turns.zh: 当真正的关口到来时，这甚至还没算上未来的生产率好处，那些将会是反通胀的，但那是以后的事。

turns.en: But I think what you're describing is another reason why I've not thrown into the towel. On the bond market, despite how painful it's been. But anybody who was in January of 2009 that said, you know what, this is ridiculous.
turns.zh: 但我认为你描述的，正是为什么尽管债市如此痛苦，我仍然没有对它认输的又一个理由。但任何一个在2009年1月说，你知道吗，这太荒唐了，

turns.en: The banks are priced for zero. You went from beginning of January of 2009 to the March lows. The S&P of 100 was down like 40%. That was the last cataclysmic.
turns.zh: 银行股被定价为零的人——你从2009年1月初一直到3月的低点，标普500跌了大约40%。那是上一次天翻地覆的时刻。

turns.en: And of course, we didn't know if TARP was going to get legislated or not. But those people in January of 2009 that bought the S&P 500, locked their nose, bought it, could withstand the next 30% or 40% down to the lows, metaling abandoned that year when you look at what happened from March to December.
turns.zh: 当然，我们当时不知道 TARP 会不会被立法通过。但那些在2009年1月买入标普500、捏着鼻子买下去、扛得住接下来那30%到40%跌到当年低点的人——当你看从3月到12月发生了什么时。

turns.en: And when people were buying the stock market in January and February of 2009, they reviewed as idiots. Now, by the way, I was bearish. I was cutting my bearish call at that point.
turns.zh: 而当人们在2009年1月和2月买入股市时，他们被视为傻瓜。顺便说一句，我当时是看空的；我正在收敛我的看空判断。

turns.en: I can't say I was turning bullish. But I thought, even at that point, I thought there were all sorts of signs of capitulation. There was fear and disdain about the stock market much like you had in the summer of 1982 when the multiple got down to eight.
turns.zh: 我不能说我当时转向看多。但我认为，即便在那个时点，我也看到了各种各样投降式抛售（capitulation）的迹象。当时股市弥漫着恐惧和鄙夷，很像1982年夏天市盈率跌到8倍时那样。

turns.en: And so I'm looking at the bond market right now the same way. I mean, it's been terrible, but it's under-owned. There's so many short positions on the board of trade and futures and options pits.
turns.zh: 所以我现在用同样的眼光看待债券市场。我是说，它一直很糟糕，但它持仓不足（under-owned）。在期货和期权交易池里有大量的空头头寸。

turns.en: And I think that everybody is just focused on inflation. And I'm not going to push back and say that, you know, that they're deranged. I just think that inflation is always in every word a very complex item to forecast.
turns.zh: 而且我认为每个人都只盯着通胀。我不会去反驳说，你知道吗，他们神志不清。我只是认为，通胀在每一个字面上都是一个非常复杂、难以预测的东西。

turns.en: There's hundreds of variables that go into it, but there's nothing I'm seeing that's telling me that we're entering into a pernicious inflationary environment.
turns.zh: 它有数百个变量参与其中，但我没有看到任何东西在告诉我，我们正在进入一个有害的通胀环境。

turns.en: Well, you just said about Chinese competition, perfect example. Build it and they will come. And you're right, there are other cheaper sources.
turns.zh: 嗯，你刚说的关于中国竞争，就是个完美的例子。建好了，他们自然会来（Build it and they will come）。而且你说得对，还有其他更便宜的来源。

turns.en: On top of that, as I said before, there's other things people aren't looking at. How come nobody's talking about the housing market in the United States?
turns.zh: 除此之外，正如我之前说的，还有别的、人们没在看的东西。怎么就没人谈谈美国的房市呢？

turns.en: Can you tell me that? And you know that Kevin Warsh, a Jackson Hole, was talked about the economy being resilient, strong and solid. It's his three favorite words.
turns.zh: 你能跟我说说这个吗？而且你知道，Kevin Warsh 在 Jackson Hole 上讲经济有韧性、强劲、稳固——那是他最爱的三个词。

turns.en: And he mentioned AI eight times. He mentioned housing once. So like I'll ask you, do you live in a data center yourself or do you live in a house?
turns.zh: 而他提到了 AI 八次，只提到了房市一次。所以我想问你，你自己是住在一个数据中心里，还是住在一栋房子里？

turns.en: Housing is in a recession. You look at the home building stocks, you think we're in a deep recession. We just got the new home sale numbers.
turns.zh: 房市正处在一场衰退里。你看那些建房股，你会以为我们正处在一场深度衰退里。我们刚拿到新房销售数据。

turns.en: The home builders are discounting their product like it's somebody's business, but we still have eight and a half months' supply of inventory.
turns.zh: 建房商在拼命打折他们的产品，打得一塌糊涂，但我们仍然有八个半月的库存供给。

turns.en: And new home prices, on average, are down eight and a half percent. I say that to people, new home prices are down eight and a half percent over the past year.
turns.zh: 而新房均价下跌了8.5%。我对人们说，新房价格在过去一年里下跌了8.5%。

turns.en: Is that a source of inflation to you? In this $50 trillion asset class called residential real estate, it's deflating. Nobody's talking about it.
turns.zh: 对你来说，那是一个通胀来源吗？在这个叫住宅房地产、规模50万亿美元的资产类别里，它正在通缩。却没人在谈它。

turns.en: And residential rents are still deflating. Nobody talks about the fact we still have a hugely overbuilt apartment market in the United States because all the multifamily construction plans from a few years ago were built on a certain level of demographics.
turns.zh: 而住宅租金也仍在通缩。没人谈这个事实：美国的公寓市场仍然严重过度建设，因为几年前所有的多户住宅（multifamily）建设计划，都是基于某个特定的人口结构水平制定的。

turns.en: And now we have no population growth in the United States because of all the outmigration. And so we still have excess supply of residential units and multifamily downward pressure on rents.
turns.zh: 而现在，由于所有那些人口外迁，美国已经没有人口增长了。所以我们仍然有住宅单元的供给过剩，以及多户住宅租金的下行压力。

turns.en: New home prices are now negative eight and a half percent year over year. If you plug those numbers in, the rents and the home prices in real time into the CPI, it'd be close to zero.
turns.zh: 新房价格如今同比是负8.5%。如果你把这些数字——租金和房价——实时代入 CPI，它会接近零。

turns.en: But the core would be well below two percent. And I think with lags, we're going to see that coming through because shelter is far more important than energy in the CPI numbers.
turns.zh: 但核心 CPI 会远低于2%。而且我认为随着滞后效应显现，我们会看到它传导过来，因为在 CPI 数据里，住所（shelter）远比能源重要。

turns.en: I'm digressing a little bit, but you're bringing up something that I think is disinflationary, not being discussed. I'm bringing up the labor market.
turns.zh: 我有点跑题了，但你提出的东西，我认为是一个没被讨论的反通胀因素。我要说的是劳动力市场。

turns.en: We've got the ADP numbers, no acceleration on wage growth whatsoever. Who's a nice headline number up 90,000? No acceleration on wages. That's very interesting to me that we have a labor market apparently, but no acceleration of wage growth.
turns.zh: 我们拿到了 ADP 数据，工资增长完全没有加速 whatsoever。谁？一个不错的标题数字，增加了9万。工资没有加速。这在我看来非常有意思：我们显然有一个劳动力市场，但工资增长却没有加速。

turns.en: That's an interesting dichotomy. And nobody's focused on the housing market, which has emerged as a source of deflation. And you mentioned the stock market.
turns.zh: 那是一种有意思的二元背离。而且没人聚焦房市，它已经浮现为一个通缩来源。你还提到了股市。

turns.en: Yes, the stock market, there is so much pain out there in white swaths of the stock market. So we can talk about the Mac 7, the AI, NVIDIA, great.
turns.zh: 是的，股市——在股市里大片的区域中，有太多的痛苦。所以我们可以谈 Mag 7、谈 AI、谈 NVIDIA，很好。

turns.en: Sure, Apple stock, great. But look at the regional banks. They've been terrible. The home builders terrible. The retailers terrible. Look at what restaurant stocks, consumer, sickle services like hotels and the cruise lines and the theme parks.
turns.zh: 当然，Apple 股票很好。但看看区域银行，它们一直很糟糕。建房商很糟糕。零售商很糟糕。看看餐饮股、消费周期服务，比如酒店、邮轮和主题公园，

turns.en: They look terrible. The small caps. So people talk, they look at the SM500 where 50% of the market cap is the 20 stocks. But nobody talks about the fact that the average and median stock in the United States is down 15% from the 52 week highs.
turns.zh: 它们看起来很糟糕。还有小盘股。所以人们盯着标普500看，那里50%的市值集中在20只股票上。但没人谈这个事实：美国股票的均值和中位数股价，已经从52周高点下跌了15%。

turns.en: They're at a correction mode. The average stock is doing, you know, people say the stock market's holding up so well, despite what the bond market's done.
turns.zh: 它们处在一种回调状态。均值股价的表现是——你知道，人们说，尽管债市那样，股市还是撑得这么好。

turns.en: No, no, there's part of the market, the big cats that seem to be impervious to interest rates. Yes, but there are white swaths of the stock market that are hurting a lot.
turns.zh: 不不，市场里有一部分，那些大市值股，似乎对利率免疫。是的，但股市中有大片区域正在遭受重创。

turns.en: So the bond market is actually having an impact, especially when you're taking a look at the areas of the SM500 that are most closely tied to Fed policy.
turns.zh: 所以债市其实正在产生影响，尤其是当你去看标普500里那些和美联储政策最紧密相关的区域时。

turns.en: They're already down 10% from the recent peak. They're in a correction mode. So for people saying to me that the Fed's having no impact, no, I think you're not looking at the right places.
turns.zh: 它们已经从近期高点回落了10%，处在回调状态。所以对于那些跟我说美联储没有产生影响的人，不，我认为你们没在看对的地方。

turns.en: So you have to dig beneath the surface to see what's going on. Speaking of places that you can dig and look for something going on, let's go to gold as a final topic.
turns.zh: 所以你得挖到表面之下去看看到底在发生什么。说到你可以挖、可以寻找动向的地方，我们把黄金作为最后一个话题来聊。

turns.en: Boy, the increasing real yields have sure clobbered gold. I don't think the fundamentals are any worse, but where's this headed? Well, you know, I wrote my first gold report when I was a Gluckenshaft back in February of 2010, and gold was $1,000 an ounce.
turns.zh: 天，不断上升的实际收益率确实重创了黄金。我不认为基本面有任何变差，但这会走向何方？嗯，你知道，我写第一份黄金报告时还在 Gluskin Sheff，那是2010年2月，当时黄金是1,000美元一盎司。

turns.en: And you know, the fundamental low around $250 an ounce was back in 1999 with the signing of the Washington Agreement that ended a decade-long period of central bank gold selling globally.
turns.zh: 而且你知道，大约250美元一盎司的那个基本面低点是在1999年，当时签署了《华盛顿协议》（Washington Agreement），结束了全球央行为期十年的黄金抛售期。

turns.en: And there's been probably a dozen big corrections along the way. Nothing moves in a straight line. Blonds definitely don't, stock markets don't, and the gold market doesn't move in a straight line either, but you're quite right that the run-up in real rates has been a serious crimp this year, and it's happened alongside the fact that a weak U.S. dollar, turner no strong U.S. dollar, and so anything priced in U.S. dollars, except oil, for obvious reasons, it's been a tough year.
turns.zh: 而这一路上大概有过十几次大回调。没有什么是直线运动的。债券肯定不是，股市不是，黄金市场也不是直线运动的；但你说得很对，实际利率的飙升今年是一个严重的掣肘，而且它发生的同时，美元从疲软转为强势，所以除了石油（出于显而易见的原因）之外，任何以美元计价的东西，今年都很难熬。

turns.en: Gold is priced in dollars, so those two important correlations, the dollar and real rates, has caused gold and silver, precious metals in general to have an off year after a great year last year. I think that this is a, we're in a corrective phase, but is the secular story over?
turns.zh: 黄金以美元计价，所以那两个重要的关联——美元和实际利率——导致黄金、白银以及贵金属整体在去年大涨之后，今年是一个不佳的年份。我认为这是一——我们处在一个回调阶段，但那个长期（secular）故事结束了吗？

turns.en: No. Now, like I said before, I started the business in October 19th, 1987. The stock market was down 22% that day, and in fact, from the August peak because of Allen Greenspan, who we ultimately called the serial bubble blower, but the maestro may he rest in peace, came in guns ablazing, just like people think worse is going to be, and the market was down 30% from the summer of 87 into the fall down 30% in a matter of months. You look at the chart today,
turns.zh: 没有。就像我之前说的，我是1987年10月19日入行的。那天股市跌了22%，而事实上，从8月的高点算起，因为 Alan Greenspan——我们最终称他为连环吹泡沫的人（serial bubble blower），但这位大师（maestro），愿他安息——一上来就火力全开，就像人们认为 Warsh 将会做的那样，市场从87年夏天到秋天跌了30%，在几个月里跌了30%。你看今天的图表，

turns.en: and he has to be 500. You can barely see it on the long-term chart. The second little bear market didn't end for till 1991. It went on for another three years. So, yeah, I think we're in a corrective phase, and I did cut our bull position in our model portfolio earlier this year, and then I started adding again in this corrective phase. The secular bull market really will end when the fundamental factor ends, and the fundamental factor is the key source of demand, which is central bank
turns.zh: 那可是标普500。你在长期图表上几乎都看不到它。第二个小熊市一直到1991年才结束，它又持续了三年。所以，是的，我认为我们处在一个回调阶段；我确实在今年早些时候削减了我们模型组合里的多头头寸，然后在这个回调阶段又开始加仓。长期牛市真正会结束的时候，是那个基本面因素结束的时候，而那个基本面因素就是需求的关键来源，也就是央行

turns.en: reserve reallocation from US dollars into a gold bullion, and global central banks continue to diversify into gold. That hasn't changed even in this period. It's been a rough period for gold for most of this year. That hasn't changed. That's the fundamental positive story. The 10-year bear market in the 1980s was nothing more than the central bank shifting to treasury bills and out of gold, to a point where the share of FX reserves and gold in the vaults at the world's
turns.zh: 把储备从美元重新配置到黄金金条，而全球央行持续多元化配置进黄金。这一点没有改变，即便在这段时间里也没有。今年大部分时间对黄金是一段艰难时期。这一点没有改变。那就是基本面的正面故事。1980年代那轮十年熊市，无非就是央行转向国库券、撤出黄金，一直到全球各

turns.en: central banks went from a higher 70% in 1980, got as low as 10% in 1999, and now we're basically about 30%. We haven't even undertaken the full mean reversion trade yet. The day I see that the central banks say we're done in this diversification, that'll be the day that the fundamental bull market ends, and we're not there yet. David, I can't thank you enough for another terrific interview, but before I let you go, I do have to push back on one thing. You gave our listeners a list of
turns.zh: 央行金库里黄金占外汇储备的份额，从1980年高达70%，降到1999年低至10%，而现在我们基本上大约在30%。我们甚至还没有完成这轮完整的均值回归交易。到我看到各央行说我们不再做这种多元化配置了的那一天，才是基本面牛市结束的那一天，而我们还没到那一步。David，我非常感谢你又一次带来一场精彩的访谈，但在我放你走之前，我确实得就一件事反驳你。你给了我们的听众一份

turns.en: important dates in the market. You left out a couple of really important ones. One September 10th, which already happened, that was the launch of the Rosie ETF in Canada on the TSX. I'm sure our listeners want to know if there's any plan to eventually launch that in any US market. The other date is October 6th. That's if you order right now when you will receive your copy of Bear in the Bullring, your new book. Please tell us about those. The book is called, as you said,
turns.zh: 市场里重要日期的清单。但你漏掉了几个真正重要的。一个是9月10日，那已经发生了，那是 Rosie ETF 在加拿大 TSX 的推出。我相信我们的听众想知道，有没有任何计划最终把它在美国的某个市场推出。另一个日期是10月6日，那是如果你现在就下单、你将收到你那本《Bear in the Bullring》、你的新书的日子。请跟我们讲讲这两件事。这本书叫，正如你说的，

turns.en: The Bear in the Bullring. It's just really a collection of ideas and themes, convictions, reflecting my life as an economist in the financial markets for the past 40 years. It's really all the collection of all those experiences and how it's shaped my philosophy, not just on the markets, but on life till this very day. Let me just say that I had a eureka moment in late 2002, 2022, when I kept on getting asked how I would grade my career. I was always too
turns.zh: 《Bear in the Bullring》。它其实就是一本想法、主题和信念的合集，反映了我作为经济学家在金融市场里过去40年的人生。它真的是所有这些经历的集合，以及它们如何塑造了我的哲学——不只是对市场的哲学，还有对人生的哲学，直到今天。我只想说，我在2022年底有过一个尤里卡时刻（eureka moment），当时人们不停地问我，我会怎么给自己的职业生涯打分。我一直太

turns.en: scared to respond. My standard answer was that if I make it to Cooperstown for economists, it will be for at bats, but probably not batting average. When people stopped chuckling at that quip, I realized I had to do something maybe a little more concrete. I said, why not just put my money where my mouth is and create a model portfolio, ETF-based, because I have 2,300 clients in 40 countries and from all different walks of the financial markets. Our research mirrors our
turns.zh: 害怕回答。我的标准答案是，如果我能进经济学家的 Cooperstown（名人堂），那会是因为我的打数（at bats），而大概不是因为我的打击率（batting average）。当人们不再对这句俏皮话咯咯笑时，我意识到我得做点也许更实在的事。我说，为什么不说到做到、身体力行，创建一个模型组合呢，基于 ETF 的，因为我在40个国家有2,300位客户，来自金融市场的各行各业。我们的研究映射了我们

turns.en: diverse client base. I said, well, why don't we create a model portfolio that mirrors the depth and the breadth of our research? I did that. It's done extremely well. It's not poorly with anything except the quality of the research at my firm. It's diversified across all asset classes and all geographies. It's unconstrained. My own client base, the same client base that pushed me to start my business in 2020, which I should really thank everybody for because it was
